figureObjective: Compare static friction before slipping with kinetic friction during sliding for the same contact pair and normal force.

claims.text: Static friction acts without relative sliding, while kinetic friction acts during relative sliding.
Static friction responds opposite the applied force up to fs(max); motion begins when the applied force exceeds that limit.
For the same contact pair, maximum static friction is usually greater than kinetic friction; this is not an exceptionless universal claim.
Friction opposes motion or attempted motion between contacting objects.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 5.4, paragraph fs-id1167066811244; official PDF page 179
anchors.exactQuote: Kinetic friction acts on an object in relative motion, while static friction acts on an object or system at rest relative to each other.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 5.4, paragraph fs-id1167066836088; official PDF page 180
anchors.exactQuote: Static friction is a responsive force that increases to be equal and opposite to whatever force is exerted, up to its maximum limit.

anchors.location: OpenStax Physics 5.4, paragraphs fs-id1167067036387, fs-id1167066879604, and fs-id1167066836088; official PDF page 180
anchors.normalizedEquation: fs <= mu_s N; fs(max) = mu_s N; fk = mu_k N

anchors.exactQuote: Frictional forces, such as f, always oppose motion or attempted motion between objects in contact.

elements.meaning: No-slip state in which static friction responds up to its maximum.
Sliding state in which kinetic friction opposes relative motion.
Applied force Fapp parallel to the common contact surface.
The same two surfaces and normal force N used in both panels.

allowedVariation.rule: The two regimes may be side-by-side or stacked if the threshold order and shared contact pair remain explicit.
Crate appearance, color, and line style may vary; force labels and arrow directions may not.
A neutral surface texture may be used only if it does not imply different materials between panels.

mutations.description: Replace the static inequality with fs = mu_s N for every static state or show fs above fs(max).
Assign kinetic friction to the no-slip panel or static friction to the sliding panel.
Point a friction arrow in the direction of motion or attempted motion.
Remove the transition threshold so the panels imply simultaneous states for the same crate.
